verses.mystical_translation: A foreign queen follows fame and questions the wisdom of the king; riches carry the scent of inquiry and longing.
Speech opens the palace; nothing of the inward court remains sealed before the inquiring mind.
Wisdom and shaped stones become a single spectacle for the stranger's eye.
Confronted by abundance and ordered life, her inward breath fails — a stunned witness before a world of display.
Report meets reality; foreign rumor becomes testimony before the throne.
Seeing revises hearing: the witnessed reality outstrips the tale.
Those near the king live in the glow of another's wisdom — both privileged and charged to listen.
The queen names the divine will behind kingship: anointed favor and purpose entwined.
Gifts measure esteem: fragrance, weight, and preciousness as diplomatic language.
Trade networks return exotic timbers and stones — crafts for temple and palace in the exchange.
Foreign wood is transformed into instruments and architecture: unfamiliar beauty enters familiar cult and court.
The exchange concludes; the traveler returns having taken and given in equal measure.
A single year's measure becomes a symbol — an exactness that invites scrutiny across witnesses.
Regional rulers and merchants alike funnel wealth into the court; trade and tribute weave the king's wealth.
Shields of beaten gold: protection fashioned from abundance, measure set in weight.
Gold as ornament and store: the forest of Lebanon becomes a repository for crafted wealth.
An ivory seat cloaked in gold: a seat that speaks both of craft and claim.
The ascent to rule is measured; lions mark the boundaries of presence and authority.
Twelve lions: an unmatched display, a royal language of power in metal and wood.
Gold saturates daily use; the ordinary measure of value is reordered by abundance.
Voyages stitch distant places to Jerusalem; exotic cargoes attest to networks beyond sight.
Flourish of riches and mind crowns a singular figure in the ancient world.
Courts travel to hear what the heart of a single ruler now holds — wisdom as a diplomatic resource.
Yearly tribute rehearses political order; each present a line in the ledger of influence.
Horse and chariot cities store military spectacle — a mobile projection of royal power.
A hegemonic claim framed by rivers and borders: the king's dominion named in geographic terms.
Plentitude transforms scarcity into abundance; words that press against credibility preserved.
Horses as imports signify connections; life at court entwined with distant stables.
The palace archive points beyond itself to prophetic records; public splendor and prophetic memory intersect.
Forty years mark a long season of rule; years counted, memory shaped.
The end of one household's grandeur; succession follows the fixed turn of the dynastic wheel.

contemplative_note: The chapter juxtaposes human splendor and foreign admiration with the fragility of perception — riches awe, yet witnesses and texts remain unsettled.
safety_note: Contains celebration of wealth, power, and political dominance; preserves morally difficult material and ambiguous wording for scholarly review.
